Question ID: BIO_U01_PT_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.BIO.SCI.01

Assessment focus: Use the stimulus exactly as written.

Plant GroupDaily LightAverage Height After 10 Days
A8 hours14 cm
B2 hours6 cm

Which statement is the strongest evidence that light amount is related to plant growth in this data set?

answer.text: Plants are alive, so light must always make them grow.

feedback.text: This choice does not use the stimulus evidence. Recheck the question, identify the mapped lesson skill, and connect the answer to the included stimulus.

answer.text: Group A received more light and had a greater average height than Group B.

feedback.text: The correct answer uses measured evidence from both groups and connects it directly to the claim about light and growth. This matches the mapped lesson content and uses the stimulus provided in the question.

answer.text: Group B had a smaller letter name than Group A.

feedback.text: This choice goes beyond what the data or model can support. Recheck the question, identify the mapped lesson skill, and connect the answer to the included stimulus.

answer.text: The table proves that light is the only factor that can ever affect plants.

feedback.text: This choice confuses a key Unit 1 term. Recheck the question, identify the mapped lesson skill, and connect the answer to the included stimulus.

Question ID: BIO_U01_PT_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.BIO.SCI.03

Assessment focus: Focus on the evidence that is measured or directly observed.

StatementSource
The sample contained tiny green cells.Microscope observation
The cells are probably algae.Student explanation

Which statement is an observation rather than an inference? Focus on the evidence that is measured or directly observed.

answer.text: The cells are probably algae. (This ignores the mapped evidence.)

feedback.text: This choice does not use the stimulus evidence. Recheck the question, identify the mapped lesson skill, and connect the answer to the included stimulus.

answer.text: The pond must be unhealthy. (This overstates the claim.)

feedback.text: This choice goes beyond what the data or model can support. Recheck the question, identify the mapped lesson skill, and connect the answer to the included stimulus.

answer.text: The student should already know the answer. (This confuses the lesson vocabulary.)

feedback.text: This choice confuses a key Unit 1 term. Recheck the question, identify the mapped lesson skill, and connect the answer to the included stimulus.

answer.text: The sample contained tiny green cells.

feedback.text: An observation is what is directly noticed or measured. Calling the cells algae is an interpretation based on the observation. This matches the mapped lesson content and uses the stimulus provided in the question.
